# Draft:RAIC Awards (1930 to 1939)

----
}}
The Royal Architectural Institute of Canada (RAIC) instituted an awards competition in 1930 to recognize “the most outstanding building designed by a member of the R.A.I.C.”  In following years, the competition amended its program to recognize the work of its member in various categories. The RAIC did not hold competitions in 1934 and 1936. In 1939, the final awards competition in this format was held. In 1950, the Governor General's Medals in Architecture program began and reinstated a national program to recognize excellence in Canadian architecture.
